mcqs.q: Bony depressions, canals and foramina on a radiograph appear:
mcqs.explain: Cavities, depressions and openings (sinus, fossa, canal, foramen) are less dense and appear radiolucent.

mcqs.q: The intermaxillary suture appears as:
opts: A thin radiolucent line in the midline (with radiopaque borders)
A radiopaque band over the molars
mcqs.explain: The intermaxillary suture is a thin radiolucent midline line (with RO borders), extending from the crest between the centrals up to the anterior nasal spine.

mcqs.q: The incisive foramen is seen as an ovoid radiolucency between the central incisor roots. A size greater than ___ should raise suspicion of an incisive canal cyst:
mcqs.explain: The incisive foramen is a midline ovoid radiolucency; if larger than 1 cm, an incisive canal cyst should be suspected.

mcqs.q: The anterior nasal spine appears as a radiopaque structure shaped like:
opts: An inverted triangle in the midline
mcqs.explain: The anterior nasal spine is a midline radiopaque inverted triangle, ~1.5–2 cm above the alveolar crest, near the base of the nasal septum.

mcqs.q: The nasal fossae appear as:
opts: Radiolucent spaces on either side of the nasal septum
mcqs.explain: The nasal fossae are radiolucent spaces (the nasal cavity) on either side of the radiopaque nasal septum.

mcqs.q: The 'inverted Y of Ennis' is formed by superimposition of the:
opts: Floor of the maxillary sinus and the floor of the nasal cavity
mcqs.explain: In canine projections, the floor of the sinus crossing the floor of the nasal cavity forms an inverted Y line (of Ennis).

mcqs.q: The maxillary sinus on a radiograph is:
opts: A dark radiolucent (air-filled) cavity with a thin radiopaque floor
mcqs.explain: The maxillary sinus is an air-filled cavity that appears radiolucent; its borders/floor are thin radiopaque lines. A septum within it can simulate a cyst.

mcqs.q: The zygomatic process of the maxilla is described as a radiopaque:
opts: 'J' or 'U' shaped line over the molars
mcqs.explain: The zygomatic process of the maxilla appears as a 'J'- or 'U'-shaped radiopaque line in the first/second molar region (with excessive vertical angulation).

mcqs.q: The maxillary tuberosity appears as:
opts: A radiopaque shadow distal to the last molar
mcqs.explain: The maxillary tuberosity is the radiopaque shadow of the maxilla next to the last molar; the pterygoid plates and hamular process lie just behind it.

mcqs.q: The genial tubercles appear as:
opts: A radiopaque ring-like shadow in the midline below the incisor roots
A dark canal below the molars
A radiopaque band over the ramus
mcqs.explain: The genial tubercles form a radiopaque ring-like shadow in the midline below the incisor roots, surrounding the lingual foramen.

mcqs.q: The lingual foramen appears as:
opts: A small radiolucent dot surrounded by the genial tubercles
mcqs.explain: The lingual foramen is a small radiolucent dot in the midline, surrounded by the radiopaque genial tubercles.

mcqs.q: Nutrient canals appear on a radiograph as:
opts: Radiolucent lines of fairly uniform width running vertically toward the apices
mcqs.explain: Nutrient canals are radiolucent lines of fairly uniform width running vertically from the inferior dental canal to a tooth apex or the interdental space.

mcqs.q: The mandibular symphysis (symphysis menti):
opts: Is a midline radiolucent line that closes by age 1 (not seen later)
mcqs.explain: The mandibular symphysis is a midline radiolucent line; it closes by about age 1 and so is not visible on later radiographs.

mcqs.q: The mental foramen is usually located:
opts: Below the apices of the premolars, between the lower border and the alveolar crest
In the midline below the incisors
mcqs.explain: The mental foramen is a radiolucent structure usually seen below the apices of the premolars, between the lower border of the mandible and the alveolar crest.

mcqs.q: The mandibular canal appears as:
opts: A dark radiolucent band with thin radiopaque superior and inferior borders, below the molar roots
mcqs.explain: The mandibular canal is a radiolucent dark shadow with thin radiopaque superior and inferior borders, seen below the molar roots.

mcqs.q: The external oblique ridge appears as a radiopaque band that is the continuation of the:
opts: Anterior border of the ramus, near the crest in the third molar region
mcqs.explain: The external oblique ridge is the continuation of the anterior border of the ramus, appearing as a radiopaque band near the alveolar crest in the third-molar region.

mcqs.q: The mylohyoid (internal oblique) ridge appears as a radiopaque band running:
opts: Diagonally downward and forward from the third molar to the premolar region
mcqs.explain: The mylohyoid (internal oblique) ridge runs diagonally downward and forward from the third molar to the premolar region.

mcqs.q: The submandibular gland fossa appears as a:
opts: Radiolucent concave area below the mylohyoid ridge
mcqs.explain: The submandibular gland fossa is a concave depression accommodating the gland; being a depression, it appears radiolucent.

mcqs.q: Which restorative materials are RADIOPAQUE?
mcqs.explain: High-density materials — amalgam, gold, silver points, pins, gutta-percha and porcelain — are radiopaque; older composites and bonding agents are radiolucent.

mcqs.q: The inferior border of the mandible appears as:
opts: A dense radiopaque band of bone
mcqs.explain: The inferior border of the mandible is a dense radiopaque band of cortical bone.

mcqs.q: The coronoid process of the mandible may appear superimposed over the maxillary third molar as a:
opts: Triangular opacity (when the radiograph is taken with the mouth closed)
mcqs.explain: The coronoid process can appear as a triangular radiopacity superimposed over the maxillary third molar region when the mouth is closed.

mcqs.q: The mental ridge appears as a radiopaque band extending from the:
mcqs.explain: The mental ridge is a radiopaque band extending from the premolar to the incisor region of the mandible.

mcqs.q: Older composite resins and bonding agents appear radiolucent because they have:
mcqs.explain: Older composites/bonding agents have lower object density, so they appear radiolucent compared with radiopaque metals and porcelain.

saqs.q: List the radiolucent landmarks of the maxillary anterior region.
saqs.a: Intermaxillary suture, incisive foramen, and the nasal fossae (the ANS and nasal septum are radiopaque).

saqs.q: Describe the maxillary sinus and zygomatic process on a radiograph.
saqs.a: Maxillary sinus = radiolucent air cavity with a thin radiopaque floor. Zygomatic process = 'J/U'-shaped radiopaque line over the molars.

saqs.q: What is the significance of an incisive foramen larger than 1 cm?
saqs.a: It should raise suspicion of an incisive canal cyst.

saqs.q: Describe the genial tubercles and lingual foramen.
saqs.a: Genial tubercles = radiopaque ring below the incisors; lingual foramen = small radiolucent dot at their centre.

saqs.q: Describe the mandibular canal and mental foramen.
saqs.a: Mandibular canal = radiolucent band with thin radiopaque borders below the molars. Mental foramen = radiolucency below the premolar apices.

saqs.q: Contrast the external oblique and mylohyoid ridges.
saqs.a: External oblique ridge = continuation of the anterior ramus border (3rd molar). Mylohyoid (internal oblique) ridge = diagonal band from 3rd molar to premolar. Both radiopaque.

saqs.q: Classify restorative materials by radiographic appearance.
saqs.a: Radiopaque: amalgam, gold, silver points, pins, gutta-percha, porcelain. Radiolucent: older composites and bonding agents.
